done_when: When the repo has a package.json, the generated forge.yml tests job sets up Node with actions/setup-node before the test command, taking the version from .nvmrc or .node-version when present, else from package.json's engines.node, else leaving the runner's default; a Python-only repo's workflow is unchanged; a test covers the three cases

findings.body: For a repository declaring `packageManager: "npm@…"` without a committed lockfile, this step fails before reaching the test command—even when that command legitimately uses `npm install && npm test` or runs dependency-free tests. setup-node v7 automatically enables npm caching and [throws when no lockfile exists](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/blob/v7/src/cache-restore.ts#L70-L80). Emit `package-manager-cache: false` so selecting Node does not introduce an unrelated lockfile requirement.
findings.title: Disable implicit npm caching in the setup-node step

why: The CI workflow Forge generates runs a Node client's tests on the runner's default Node, so a client that requires another version fails npm ci (a copied-in client needs Node 24, the runner has 22)
